newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland stadium COPs issue set for mid May.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland stadium COPs issue set for mid May.

text.p: Cleveland plans to sell $130 million certificates of participation (COPs) in mid May to help finance the stadium for its future expansion National Football League Browns franchise, the city's finance director said.
In January, Cleveland had planned to issue the debt on about April 1 for the new stadium which will occupy the same site as the old Municipal Stadium, Martin Carmody told Reuters on Monday.

With a "comfortable cushion" of funds on hand to finance the current construction needs, Cleveland opted to put off the sale for a few weeks until about May 15 to wrap up details on the documents and get a final determination on how much money the NFL will contribute to the stadium, Carmody said.

The NFL is expected to contribute about $48 million for stadium construction costs, although an exact figure has not been nailed down, Carmody said. The whole stadium cost has been estimated at about $242.8 million, he noted.
The COPs are to be paid off with revenues from taxes on parking, admissions and car rentals. A.G. Edwards & Sons has been selected to lead the syndicate for the offering.
Carmody said Monday that it is "highly likely" that the COPs will be insured by AMBAC as well.

In October, Cleveland sold $15 million of bond anticipation notes (BANs) to fund demolition of Municipal Stadium, where the former Cleveland Browns played before their move to Baltimore where they became the Ravens.
The BANs may be rolled over during the construction phase and then, at the conclusion of construction, they may be taken out at that point, Carmody said.
The Browns announced in January that they had met their seat sales goal for the franchise to begin play in 1999. Waiting a few weeks to sell the COPs will not change that time schedule, Carmody said.
Last week, Cleveland awarded a contract for mass excavation of the site and driving of pilings for the new stadium, Carmody said.
